rooms.question: Can a population change without a single specimen being named the best?
rooms.ontology: Variation and reproduction can change a population without an explicit ranked fitness score. Survival still depends on implemented resources and constraints.
rooms.action: Follow a few different bodies in the small field, then compare the population, birth and death counts over time.
rooms.observable: Bodies wander, expend energy, gain energy in previously unvisited cells, reproduce above an energy threshold, and die at zeroenergy.
rooms.mechanism: The default drift model starts30creatures, tracks visits on20×20cells and mutates child size, speed and colour. Exploration yieldsenergy; reproduction splits it. Other selection configurations are static composed terminalstates.
rooms.limit: No ranked objective does not mean no selection pressure. Energy for novelty, decay and populationcaps favour some behaviour over others.
rooms.variation: Existing: watch persistence without choosing a champion. Proposed: expose the exploration reward and compare which bodies persist; curator uniform/culled modes are illustrations, not evolved results.
rooms.prior_bridge: The previous ecosystem made its stabilizer visible; now inspect the conditions hidden in a claim of goal-free evolution.
rooms.next_bridge: The next room makes an explicit numerical objective into a landscape.

sources.fact: Only drift mode simulates; other modes hold composed states.

cautions: Source-reviewed draft; current museum reach, readable labels, controls and human learning unverified.

rooms.question: Will the same observations lead to the same best fit when error is measured differently?
rooms.ontology: A loss assigns a number to modelparameters. Here each terrain is a function of slope w and intercept b for the same small dataset.
rooms.action: Watch the three balls descend their labelled terrains. Change Outliers, then watch where each path travels; use the reset button for another run.
rooms.observable: MSE, Huber and the third oscillating loss produce different surfaces and paths. The Outliers knob regenerates the data and restarts balls at the same parameterpair.
rooms.mechanism: MSE squares residuals; Huber is quadratic nearzero and linear beyond1; the third loss averages sin(3e)+.5e². Finitedifferences estimate the two gradients and a fixedlearningrate steps downhill inside[-2,2]².
rooms.limit: A minimum is relative to the chosen penalty and model. The artifact label adversarial names a custom wavyloss, not GAN training or adversarial robustness.
rooms.variation: Existing: add outliers and ask which deviations each loss discounts or magnifies. Proposed: mark whose observations become outliers instead of treating that designation as selfevident.
rooms.prior_bridge: Evolution varied bodies without derivatives; this room varies parameters using local slope.
rooms.next_bridge: Classification asks what forms of grouping and decision the objective produces.
cautions: Source-reviewed draft; current museum reach, readable labels, controls and human learning unverified.

rooms.question: When points share a colour, has a group been discovered or assigned?
rooms.ontology: K-means alternates nearest-centroid assignment with moving each centroid to its assigned points mean; k is chosen in advance.
rooms.action: Choose one point near the boundary between colours. Watch its assignment and the neighbouring centroid move through automatic iterations.
rooms.observable: Centroids move and point colours can change. Motion stops when totalcentroid movement falls below the threshold or50iterations are reached.
rooms.mechanism: Default4centroids compete for100points from a generated dataset with3natural clusters plusnoise. Assignment uses Euclideandistance; update uses arithmeticmeans.
rooms.limit: This is unsupervisedclustering, not supervisedclassification. Colours do not name natural or ethical categories. The displayed totaldistance sums ordinary distances although textbook k-means minimizes squared distances.
rooms.variation: Existing: compare a peripheralpoint to a centralpoint. Proposed: expose k or curate ring/braid cohorts to ask whether the mean-and-distance rule preserves the grouping the visitor sees.
rooms.prior_bridge: Loss shaped a numerical fit; now a repeated local rule assigns membership.
rooms.next_bridge: A neuralnetwork distributes an adjustable computation across several layers.

sources.fact: Nearestassignment, arithmeticmean update and stopping rule.
Automatic iteration default; keyboard/UI controls not VRcontrols.

cautions: Source-reviewed draft; current museum reach, readable labels, controls and human learning unverified.
Scene/map use0.6scale; no hand-driven pointedit or museum UI usability verified.

rooms.question: What changes in a network when its answers become closer to the examples?
rooms.ontology: A neuron computes an activation from weightedinputs plusbias. Backpropagation distributes outputerror into parameterupdates across layers.
rooms.action: Follow one connection while watching the epoch/error display during automatic training. Compare its appearance early and later; also inspect the direction from inputs tooutputs.
rooms.observable: Weighted links and activations change as actual batches update weights/biases; the error history records the batcherror, which need not decrease on every step.
rooms.mechanism: The scene implements forward_pass, backward_pass and batchgradient accumulation on a four-example4input/2output XOR-like dataset. Positive/negative weights use differentcolours; default auto_train begins a timer.
rooms.limit: Fitting four examples cannot establish generalintelligence or out-of-distribution reliability. A visible network diagram omits the choice of examples and targetlabels.
rooms.variation: Existing: track a connection that changes sign or strength. Proposed: compare heldout inputs or a curator topology change while retaining the same examples.
rooms.prior_bridge: Centroids concentrated a group into means; networks build a succession of learned transforms.
rooms.next_bridge: Perception next asks which local features are extracted and which labels merely asserted.

sources.fact: Real forward/backward calculations update weights andbiases.

cautions: Source-reviewed draft; current museum reach, readable labels, controls and human learning unverified.
Do not confuse with placed NeuralNetworks_VR whose loss is timed animation. Desktop R/T/space handled but not a verified sharedmuseum interaction.

rooms.question: Which parts of this display were computed from pixels, and which were supplied as names?
rooms.ontology: A local filter combines pixelvalues to produce a featuremap. Objectclassification is a separate inference from that numericaloperation.
rooms.action: Compare the input cross/circle to its edgeimage. Follow the moving3×3window, then inspect the objectboxes and percentages.
rooms.observable: Broad bright interiors give way to edge responses at changes. The window tours locations; the named detectionboxes are also visible, but their percentages are fixed labels.
rooms.mechanism: Sobel x/y kernels compute gradientmagnitude, clamped0–1, on the16×16input; borderpixels becomezero. Circle92% and Cross85% are authored constants, not outputs of a fitteddetector.
rooms.limit: A confidentcaption is not a measurement. A real localedge computation does not automatically justify the objectnames next toit.
rooms.variation: Existing: point out an imagefeature that contributes to anedge yet has no namedbox. Proposed: visitor pixelpainting wired to the existing setter, or curator invented boxes on unchangeddata.
rooms.prior_bridge: The previousroom actually fitted exampletargets; here separate numerical transformation from asserted recognition.
rooms.next_bridge: Sequence models next represent relationships through time.
cautions: Source-reviewed draft; current museum reach, readable labels, controls and human learning unverified.
Labels invite painting but handevents are not wired in inspectedscript. Filter API always appliesSobel; do not promise alternatefilters or classification accuracy.

rooms.question: What would a memory need to keep, admit and reveal separately?
rooms.ontology: An LSTM distinguishes persistent cellstate, newinput and output; gates weight retention, writing and reading. This room provides a spatialdiagram of those roles.
rooms.action: Locate FORGET, INPUT and OUTPUT spheres and follow the particlepath through thecell. Compare the roles before reading their names as a memoryalgorithm.
rooms.observable: A stream crosses thecell and gateobjects change visualintensity with activation. The current stream continues independently of the gateactivations.
rooms.mechanism: The script maps gate worldheight to0–1activation, but memoryparticles follow a timed sinusoidalpath; no recurrentstate computation or traininggradient is connected to thatpath.
rooms.limit: A moving memorymetaphor does not demonstrate retaining a sequence. Gateobjects are RigidBody3D with collisionlayers; successful museum grabbing has not beenestablished.
rooms.variation: Proposed nextbuild: expose a shorttoken sequence, a numericcellstate and gatecontrols that causally alter it; compare preserving an inconvenient input with forgetting it.
rooms.prior_bridge: Perception extracted spatialfeatures; this diagram asks what a model must retain betweeninputs.
rooms.next_bridge: Generation next turns from reporting a sequence to proposingnew samples.
cautions: Source-reviewed draft; current museum reach, readable labels, controls and human learning unverified.
Only claim observationaldiagram. The promised retentionexperiment remains a buildgap; do not make grabbing prerequisite for reading.

rooms.question: Who judges a generated example, and how could that judgement change its maker?
rooms.ontology: A generator proposes samples and a discriminator judges samples relative to trainingdata. Their coupled objectives make a feedbackloop; this artifact diagrams itsroles.
rooms.action: Move your viewpoint between generator and discriminator, then trace the labelled feedbackroute and compare the two displayedlosses.
rooms.observable: Separatezones, samplemarks, a feedbackloop and a competitionpillar animate. Generatorloss falls and discriminatorloss oscillates in thedisplay.
rooms.mechanism: Both losses and quality are computed from elapsedtime/training_progress; feedbackparticles orbit rather than transmit calculatedgradients. No learnedgenerator/discriminator is implementedhere.
rooms.limit: The diagram can locate the roles but cannot establish that samples improve, that judging works or that the system reached equilibrium. Similarappearance is not evidence of training.
rooms.variation: Proposed: a small realdataset, generatedsample and discriminator score linked by anactual update; allow visitor disagreement with the selected examples ofrealness.
rooms.prior_bridge: Memory asked what is retained; generation asks what can be proposed from what wasretained.
rooms.next_bridge: The synthesis asks what an algorithm measures before giving authority to itsjudgement.

sources.fact: Losses derive from time rather thanlearning.

cautions: Source-reviewed draft; current museum reach, readable labels, controls and human learning unverified.
Do not claim visitor judging/noisethrowing trains aGAN. Thismap needs a causalexperiment beyond diagram coverage.

rooms.question: Is a point unusual by itself, or unusual under a particular measuringrule?
rooms.ontology: An anomaly score measures departure from a reference; a threshold turns that score into a decision.
rooms.action: Find one raised highlightedpoint and one unraisedpoint. Compare their positions to the maincloud and read the displayed mode/threshold.
rooms.observable: Points meeting the active threshold rise.25units and scale1.35; the summary counts flaggedpoints. Default mode is Z-score and threshold2.4.
rooms.mechanism: Z-score here is the sum of absolute standardizedx/y deviations. Samples include72Gaussianpoints and10deliberateouterpoints; mean andspread are computed over allsamples.
rooms.limit: Flagging is a relation to thisdataset and chosenrule, not proof that an event or person iswrong. Other named modes are heuristics; autoencoder_error is a handwritten sinusoidalresidual, not a trainedautoencoder.
rooms.variation: Proposed: wire existing mode/threshold APIs into visitorcontrols and retain the samepoint while its designation changes. Untilthen compare the visiblepoint positions in the defaultmode.
rooms.prior_bridge: After a generatordiagram, demand a traceable link between displayedjudgement and implementedcalculation.
rooms.next_bridge: Graph theory next makes relationships themselves the data.
cautions: Source-reviewed draft; current museum reach, readable labels, controls and human learning unverified.
No VRcontrol is wired for mode/threshold; do not instruct knob use.
